ignorePaths.justification: Inert synthetic test fixtures: they reproduce IOC names, malicious-shaped lifecycle scripts, lockfiles and workflows so every check has a positive control. Nothing in them is installed or run by GitHub, and wormsign diff still checks manifests, local actions and package-manager config under ignored paths.
Golden SARIF and JSON outputs of scans over test/fixtures; they quote the fixtures' inert indicators by design.
The sourced IOC data the scanner matches against. It must hold every indicator verbatim, so scanning it would only report the IOC list itself.

entries.justification: test/iocs-data.test.ts holds a published exfiltration endpoint (the 2025-09 webhook.site URL) as a string, to prove the IOC data stores it defanged and the loader refangs it. It is test input, never requested.
test/checks.test.ts uses a made-up webhook.site URL as input to the generic-endpoint check (WS-EX-001); nothing requests it.
test/checks.test.ts uses a made-up webhook.site URL to prove node_modules mode skips generic endpoints; nothing requests it.
test/scanner-hardening.test.ts uses an upper-case made-up webhook.site URL to prove endpoint matching ignores case; nothing requests it.
test/scanner-hardening.test.ts builds 20,000 made-up webhook.site URLs to prove the exfil check stays linear; nothing requests them.
test/scanner-wiring.test.ts writes a made-up webhook.site URL into a temporary project to prove the scanner wiring reports it; nothing requests it.
test/cli-consistency.test.ts uses a made-up webhook.site URL to prove that an IOC endpoint below medium does not replace the medium generic finding (WS-EX-001); nothing requests it.

docs/evidence/data/fp-corpus.json is the false-positive study's output. It quotes the WS-EX-001 finding the scan reported in astro's unit test (a made-up ngrok host used as an Origin header value, classified as a false positive in docs/evidence/false-positives.md). It is recorded data; nothing requests it.
